recipes.name: Rich and Creamy Potatoes au Gratin
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and very thinly sliced
freshly ground black pepper to taste
2 cups freshly shredded Gruyere cheese, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place potatoes, garlic, and salt into a large pot; fill with enough water to cover. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium and simmer potatoes until tender but not mushy, 8 to 10 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer about half the potatoes into a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Pour 1/2 of the cream over the potatoes and season with black pepper and nutmeg; sprinkle 1/2 of the Gruyère cheese on top. Layer the remaining potatoes on top and season with black pepper and nutmeg. Pour over remaining cream and sprinkle with remaining Gruyère cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is golden brown on top, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Rich and Creamy Potatoes au Gratin
raw_recipe.description: This cheesy potato au gratin with Gruyère bakes layers of potato slices in a rich and creamy sauce for an indulgent side dish that no one can resist.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make a recipe for au gratin potatoes with Gruyère — a delicious and easy-to-make side dish. To make it, thinly slice three pounds of Yukon Gold potatoes, boil them with garlic and salt until tender, and layer them in a baking dish with heavy cream, nutmeg, and fresh shredded Gruyere cheese. The resulting casserole is a rich and creamy side dish, perfect for any occasion.

review.reviewBody: For those of you who are hesitant to try this recipe because of the cost of Gruyere, I have a tip. Grate cheap grocery store brand Swiss cheese; it costs roughly $3 per pound instead of $18 or so per pound like Gruyere. Then pour about 3 T. of white wine over the 2 C. of the Swiss, toss, and let sit for at least 15 minutes. When ready to use, blot with a paper towel to remove excess wine, and it will remarkably cook up just like Gruyere. Your palate won't know the difference, but your pocketbook will!

Potato perfection. I chose to slice my potatoes a little thicker, perhaps between 1/8 and 1/4 inch, and only boiled them a few minutes to ensure they would not be reduced to mush. I’d do so exactly the same next time. These are, indeed, rich and creamy and develop a beautiful and extra delicious golden brown crust as they bake. I loved the subtle flavor of the nutmeg (fresh does make a big difference I believe), which was an ideal choice to enhance, just slightly, the flavor of the potatoes as well as that gorgeous Gruyere cheese. Not only were these a decadent taste sensation, they were remarkably easy to assemble as well – no sauce to prepare, just layer cream and cheese! After sampling these it will be interesting to see if I ever go back to traditional au gratin potatoes prepared with cheddar again.

My wife’s absolute favorite dish. And at the risk of tooting my own horn I make her quite a few delicious dishes. This is good because it’s relatively easy for me to throw together when she asks for it. Pro tip - get your Gruyère cheese at Costco. Big blocks of it for a lot less money. I always increase the quantities. A full pint of cream, 4+ lbs of taters, enough cheese to cover each layer. I go 3 layers with the added ingredients. I also increase the garlic and run the water through a strainer to catch all the garlic which gets dispersed throughout the dish. So good!!!

1. Not crazy about boiling the potatoes, garlic salt first; but it might save time in the oven. 2. If it's bland, two easy fixes: mix crushed anchovies (up to a can) into the cream; add caramelized sliced onions as a layer. 3. Nothing's better than Gruyere for this recipe, but Swiss or a Swiss combo or Fontina (mixed with Gruyere or not) should work perfectly.

I used what I had on hand which was sweet potatoes, Yukon golds and russet potatoes to make 3 lbs. I blanched the thin slices of potato but only for 3 minutes. They then went into an ice bath to stop the cooking. I used salt, nutmeg and pepper on the two layers along with Gruyère,a little cheddar I had and Parmesan cheese on top. When it came out of the oven I topped with green onion and chives. Best potato casserole ever.

I used closer to 1.5 cups of heavy cream and I mixed 1/2 cup of white wine into the cream. I layered the potatoes with a little minced Garlic. I also used some extra cheese. They took about an hour to cook. I undercovered them for the last 20 min to brown. Delicious.
we added about 6oz of regular cream cheese and it really enhanced the creaminess of the sauce. mixed it with the heavy cream and heated it up so I could blend it together easily.

This was delicious. I also skipped the boiling part in Step 2 and just went straight to layering in the baking dish. Only other alteration was adding sliced yellow onion. Everyone loved this dish, I think someone might have licked the baking dish at the end.

I always read reviews before a try a recipe. Based on what I read, I did not boil the potatoes first. I used a mixture of Gruyere, Swiss, and white cheddar cheese (1 LB Gruyere, 1/2 LB each of the other two, I used 5 LB of potatoes because of the number of people I was feeding). I also increased the amount of heavy cream. The only other change I made was to use smoked paprika instead of nutmeg, just a personal preference. Everyone LOVED it!! It was so good. Next time I may add some thinly sliced onions too, just because that sounds good to me!

Excellent! The first time I made it exactly as instructed. It was definitely lacking salt, for which I’d deduct a half a star if I could. The second time, I added some thinly sliced onions, the salt to both layers, and I skipped the boiling and just baked it. Onions or not onions, I recommend salt and skipping the boiling to save a dirty pot.

Really liked he rustic look of these potatoes, but they need SALT. I layered salt, pepper and nutmeg between and on top, and I still thought they needed salt when served (and I'm not a big salt fan). At 6,000 feet above sea level, it takes longer to boil water so I waited until my water was boiling, added the potatoes for 5 minutes - they were perfectly done. Hint: get all the potatoes sliced, then add them at the same time to the water for consistent cooking.
I wasn't crazy with the taste. The cheese wasn't my favorite. Everyone else loved it.
Great recipe! Fast and delicious I just change the cheese up and use aged yellow cheddar cheese.

I was out of nutmeg, so subbed smoked paprika, different but still delicious. This will be on regular rotation, we always have Gruyère on hand, & this is one of the best recipes I’ve encountered for it. I added onion and frozen spinach. Ohhh la-la!
Very good and easy recipe Everyone loved them I used whited cheddar , and Swiss cheese As well as Parmesan on top ! Yummy
You should add and very delicious to the title. Creamy is an understatement. It's summer here and I'm sweating, so not repeating until winter :) because it's pretty hot.
Really yummy. I did skip one step. I cut the potatoes very thin, didn't boil them and just cooked them a bit longer. Maybe that's why it wasn't runny for me.
I made it with smoked gouda and New York cheddar with onion cheeses. It was amazing! Next time, I will add mushrooms!
This was an awesome dish! it was creamy and vary flavorful. would highly recommend this recipe!!!!
I cut the recipe in half, do I still need to bake it for 1 hour or half that?
